name: Maximum Projected Teaching Set Size
definition: The **Maximum Projected Teaching Set Size** is the largest teaching-set size attained by a concept in any coordinate projection of $\mathcal{H}$. It is equivalently the star number.
graph_summary: Largest teaching-set size of a concept over all coordinate projections; equal to the star number.

monotonic.proof: For every coordinate projection, the projected subfamily is a subfamily of the projected original class. Maximum teaching-set size cannot increase under that restriction; maximize over projections.

p_monotonic.proof: A projection of a projection is a projection of the original class. The defining maximum over all projections therefore cannot increase after restricting to one projection.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: This parameter equals Star Number. The six-concept Star-Number counterexample $\{001,010,011,100,101,110\}$ has equal value 2 on the full class and on both fibres of its last coordinate.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: This parameter equals Star Number. Tight strict c-monotonicity would imply strict c-monotonicity, which fails on the transferred six-concept counterexample.

strictly_monotonic.proof: This parameter equals Star Number. Strict monotonicity requires strict c-monotonicity, which fails on the transferred six-concept counterexample.
